_about.policy: Every number in a profile is one of MEASURED (BT5 put a probe sequence through the vendor's own order-entry checker and recorded the verdict), PUBLISHED (the vendor states it on a page we link), or INHERITED (carried from a sibling product of the SAME vendor, never across vendors). A profile's `notes` field says which, in prose, for the reader of a finding; this file records the source for the reader of the code.
_about.why_in_lane: Liability-flagging vendor data, so it lives beside the module under M4's ownership rather than in root data/. Nothing here changes a protein.
_about.recalibration: Vendor numbers drift -- Twist moved its published homopolymer limit from 14 to 30 bp between 2023 and 2026. Re-run the ladder and re-read the pages on the cadence in docs/design/vendor-gc-calibration.md, and move `last_verified` only when you actually looked.

adapters.notes: "Adapter sequences are not added by default to Gene Fragments." Adapter-on is a separate checkout option, carried as its own profile.

length_bp.notes: The 300 bp FLOOR is the bound users are surprised by. Clonal genes, not fragments, are what reach 7 kb.

homopolymer.notes: STALE-LEANING AND DELIBERATELY TIGHT. The brief recorded 'under 14 bp', which is the 2023 number; the current FAQ says 30 bp. Neither is stated for the Gene Fragment product specifically. Kept at 13 because E1 is HARD_LATTICE: loosening it on an unverified number fails SILENTLY, since a lattice constraint's output when a run is permitted is the absence of a finding. Open question for the next recalibration.

global_gc.notes: 18-probe ladder through the Twist order form: <=25% Not Accepted, 30-80% all Standard, including 80%. Floor 0.28 splits the refused 25% from the accepted 30%.

adapters.notes: DATED TWICE OVER: these are the adapters for orders placed after 2021-11-02. An older order carries a different pair.

length_bp.notes: Same product, different checkout option. See e9_length_tiers for the unresolved question of whether the bound applies to the insert or the insert plus these 44 bp -- E9 reports the disagreement rather than guessing.
The only configured product that accepts an insert under 300 bp, which is what makes it the alternative E9 names for a short design.

homopolymer.notes: ~10 consecutive A/T but only ~6 consecutive G/C. The asymmetry is the point: it is the clearest vendor evidence that G/C runs are chemically worse rather than merely repetitive (G-quadruplex formation on the solid support), and a single 'max homopolymer' number would encode the wrong physics. These are the tightest run limits in the registry, which is why DEFAULT_VENDOR resolves here.

global_gc.notes: 18-probe ladder through the gBlocks plate-entry complexity checker: <=25% Denied, 30-65% clean, 70-75% Accepted-Moderate (an acceptance with a surcharge), 80% Denied. The ceiling 0.77 is the solved Denied threshold from the penalty line score = 1.40*GC%-83.8, fit on three exact hits. IDT's own STATED target is 32-62%, which is a soft scored preference and not where they refuse -- the measurement is what is encoded.

homopolymer.notes: Same vendor, different product line. eBlocks publish their own design guidelines and these have not been read against them.

global_gc.notes: The calibration ladder was run through gBlocks plate entry only, so this is one IDT product's measurement applied to another. Inheriting inside a vendor is the policy; nothing is carried across one, because the ladder's finding IS that Twist ships 80% as Standard where IDT denies it.

genscript.why: Out of scope -- BT5 spec's gene fragments from Twist and IDT -- and it had no adapters and no length range, so it could never become a complete profile. VendorProfile now refuses a half-filled one on principle.

twist_standard.why: Not a product. 'Standard' is the complexity VERDICT the Twist checker returns, so this key named a tier while the adapter/length namespace next to it named a product. Its numbers moved to twist_gene_fragment; the key is gone.
